newsitem.title: CANADA: TELUS exemption appealed with Canada cabinet.
newsitem.headline: TELUS exemption appealed with Canada cabinet.

text.p: An association of specialty television channels appealed to the Canadian cabinet on Monday to overturn a regulatory decision that it said could enable TELUS Corp to carry fewer specialty services.

The appeal was made by the Specialty and Premium Television Association (SPTV), representing 80 percent of Canada's specialty and premium television services by revenue, a group that has benefited from rules requiring specialty channels to be bundled in with more popular channels.

It said the decision by the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission -- which granted Telus's wholly owned Telus Cable Holdings Inc a license for broadcast distribution on a trial basis -- exempted Telus from distribution and linkage rules for Canadian distributors.
Linkage rules call for a minimum of Canadian specialty and premium services to be included in each marketing package offered to consumers.
SPTV President Jane Logan said the group welcomed experimentation with technology.

"We must be careful, however, not to abandon a policy approach that has given rise to one of Canada's most vibrant and expanding industries. This decision creates a de facto change to that policy," she said in announcing the appeal.
The group said that no exemption was sought in a similar trial being conducted by Bell Canada of BCE Inc.
It also said that cable distributor Shaw Communications Inc already applied for the same relief from distribution and linkage rules in Calgary on the basis of competitive fairness.
"We have no ability to pre-judge the outcome of the Shaw application or others like it in the future," Logan said.
"As a result, we are left with no choice but to appeal and seek a reaffirmation of the existing rules and the policy approach that they represent."
